```{r Baseline and Monthly Predictions — Tuned BRT + ESM Species}
  	)

  	ESM_SPECIES <- c(
  		"Aedes aegypti", "Aedes geniculatus",
  		"Anopheles maculipennis", "Anopheles plumbeus", "Anopheles sacharovi",
  		"Culex tritaeniorhynchus", "Culiseta annulata", "Culiseta longiareolata",
  		"Hyalomma aegyptium", "Rhipicephalus sanguineus"
  	)

	## Taxon-to-covariate mapping
  	TUNED_BRT_MOSQUITO <- c("Aedes vexans", "Culex theileri")
  	TUNED_BRT_TICK     <- c("Haemaphysalis inermis", "Hyalomma marginatum")
  	ESM_TICK           <- c("Hyalomma aegyptium", "Rhipicephalus sanguineus")

	## Covariate sets (must match layer names in raster stacks)
  	MOSQUITO_COVARIATES <- c(
  		"hurs", "pr", "sfcWind", "tas", "tasmax", "tasmin",
  		"NDVI", "Elevation", "Slope", "WorldCover"
  	)

  	TICK_COVARIATES <- c(
  		"hurs", "pr", "tas", "tasmax", "tasmin",
  		"NDVI", "Elevation", "Slope",
  		"BulkDensity", "CoarseFragments", "Nitrogen",
  		"SoilpH", "SandContent", "SiltContent", "SoilOrganicCarbon",
  		"WorldCover"
  	)

	## Clean month labels from the monthly_rasters list names
	## Converts "Georgia_Covariates_Jan" → "Jan", etc.
  	MONTH_LABELS <- gsub("Georgia_Covariates_", "", names(monthly_rasters))
  	names(MONTH_LABELS) <- names(monthly_rasters)

	## Ordered month sequence for consistent output
  	MONTH_ORDER <- c("Jan", "Feb", "Mar", "Apr", "May", "Jun",
  	                 "Jul", "Aug", "Sep", "Oct", "Nov", "Dec")


# HELPER FUNCTIONS

	#' Get the correct covariate vector for a given species
  	get_covariates_for_species <- function(sp_name) {
  		if (sp_name %in% c(TUNED_BRT_MOSQUITO)) return(MOSQUITO_COVARIATES)
  		if (sp_name %in% c(TUNED_BRT_TICK))     return(TICK_COVARIATES)
  		if (sp_name %in% ESM_TICK)               return(TICK_COVARIATES)
  		## Default: ESM mosquitoes
  		return(MOSQUITO_COVARIATES)
  	}


	#' Prepare a raster for BRT prediction by subsetting layers and factoring WorldCover
  	prepare_raster_for_brt <- function(rast_stack, covariates) {
  
  		## Subset to the covariates this species needs
  		  proj_raster <- rast_stack[[covariates]]
  
  		## Ensure WorldCover is treated as a factor
    		if ("WorldCover" %in% names(proj_raster)) {
    			proj_raster[["WorldCover"]] <- as.factor(proj_raster[["WorldCover"]])
    		}
  
  		return(proj_raster)
  	}


	#' Generate mean + SD prediction from a list of 100 BRT models
	#' Returns a two-layer SpatRaster (mean, sd) on the probability scale
  	predict_brt_ensemble <- function(model_list, proj_raster) {
  
  		## Predict from each valid model
    		pred_stack <- model_list |>
    			compact() |>
    			map(function(mod) {
    				tryCatch({
    					terra::predict(
    						proj_raster,
    						mod,
    						n.trees = mod$gbm.call$best.trees,
    						type    = "response",
    						na.rm   = TRUE
    					)
    				}, error = function(e) {
    					warning("  Single BRT prediction failed: ", e$message)
    					return(NULL)
    				})
    			}) |>
    			compact() |>
    			rast()

  		## Pixel-wise mean and SD across the 100 models
  		  mean_rast <- app(pred_stack, mean, na.rm = TRUE)
  		  sd_rast   <- app(pred_stack, sd,   na.rm = TRUE)
  
  		## Name the layers for consistency with existing output convention
  		  names(mean_rast) <- "mean"
  		  names(sd_rast)   <- "sd"
  
  		return(c(mean_rast, sd_rast))
  	}


	#' Run ecospat ESM projection + ensemble projection for one raster surface
	#' Returns a single-layer SpatRaster on the 0–1 probability scale
  	project_esm_to_raster <- function(esm_model, esm_ensemble, proj_raster) {
  
  		## Bivariate projections (one per predictor pair)
    		biv_proj <- ecospat.ESM.Projection(
    			ESM.modeling.output = esm_model,
    			new.env             = proj_raster,
    			parallel            = FALSE
    		)
  
  		## Weighted ensemble across bivariate models (0–1000 scale)
    		ens_proj <- ecospat.ESM.EnsembleProjection(
    			ESM.prediction.output       = biv_proj,
    			ESM.EnsembleModeling.output = esm_ensemble
    		)
  
  		## Rescale from 0–1000 to 0–1 probability
  		  ens_proj <- ens_proj / 1000
  
  		  names(ens_proj) <- "mean"
  
  		  return(ens_proj)
  	}


# PART 1: TUNED BRT PREDICTIONS (4 species × 100 models each)

  	purrr::walk(TUNED_BRT_SPECIES, function(sp) {
  
  		sp_clean   <- gsub(" ", "_", sp)
  		covariates <- get_covariates_for_species(sp)
  		sp_start   <- Sys.time()
  
  		cat("───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n")
  		cat("SPECIES:", sp, "\n")
  		cat("  Covariates:", length(covariates), "\n")
  
  		## Load saved model objects (list of 100 gbm.step objects)
  		model_path <- file.path(
  			TUNED_BRT_MODEL_DIR,
  			paste0(sp_clean, "_tuned_brt_models.rds")
  		)
  
  		if (!file.exists(model_path)) {
  			cat("  ⚠ Model file not found:", model_path, "\n")
  			cat("  Skipping this species.\n\n")
  			return(invisible())
  		}
  
  		models <- readRDS(model_path)
  		n_valid <- sum(!map_lgl(models, is.null))
  		cat("  Loaded", n_valid, "valid models out of", length(models), "\n")
  
  
  		## ── Baseline prediction ──────────────────────────────────────────
  		cat("  Predicting baseline...\n")
  
  		baseline_proj <- prepare_raster_for_brt(baseline_raster, covariates)
  		baseline_pred <- predict_brt_ensemble(models, baseline_proj)
  
  		writeRaster(
  			baseline_pred,
  			file.path(PREDICTION_DIR, "Baseline", paste0(sp_clean, "_baseline.tif")),
  			overwrite = TRUE
  		)
  
  		cat("    ✓ Baseline saved (",
  		    round(minmax(baseline_pred[["mean"]])[2], 3), "max prob )\n")
  
  
  		## ── Monthly predictions ──────────────────────────────────────────
  		cat("  Predicting monthly surfaces...\n")
  
  		## Create species-specific monthly output folder
  		monthly_sp_dir <- file.path(PREDICTION_DIR, "Monthly", sp_clean)
  		dir.create(monthly_sp_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
  
  		## Iterate across months in calendar order
  		purrr::walk(MONTH_ORDER, function(month_label) {
  
  			## Find the matching raster key in monthly_rasters
  			raster_key <- paste0("Georgia_Covariates_", month_label)
  
  			if (!raster_key %in% names(monthly_rasters)) {
  				cat("    ⚠ Missing raster for:", month_label, "\n")
  				return(invisible())
  			}
  
  			month_proj <- prepare_raster_for_brt(
  				monthly_rasters[[raster_key]], covariates
  			)
  			month_pred <- predict_brt_ensemble(models, month_proj)
  
  			writeRaster(
  				month_pred,
  				file.path(monthly_sp_dir, paste0(sp_clean, "_", month_label, ".tif")),
  				overwrite = TRUE
  			)
  
  			cat("    ✓", month_label, "\n")
  		})
  
  		## Free memory
  		rm(models, baseline_proj, baseline_pred)
  		gc()
  
  		elapsed <- round(difftime(Sys.time(), sp_start, units = "mins"), 1)
  		cat("  Done (", elapsed, "min )\n\n")
  	})


# PART 2: ESM PREDICTIONS (10 species)
  	
	purrr::walk(ESM_SPECIES, function(sp) {

		sp_clean <- gsub(" ", "_", sp)
		sp_start <- Sys.time()

		## Load saved ESM model objects
		  model_path <- file.path(ESM_MODEL_DIR, sp_clean, "esm_model_objects.rds")

  		if (!file.exists(model_path)) {
  			cat("  ⚠ Model file not found:", model_path, "\n")
  			cat("  Skipping this species.\n\n")
  			return(invisible())
  		}

  		esm_objs     <- readRDS(model_path)
  		esm_model    <- esm_objs$esm_model
  		esm_ensemble <- esm_objs$esm_ensemble
  		covariates   <- esm_objs$covariates

		## ── Baseline prediction ──────────────────────────────────────────

		## Subset baseline raster to the covariates the ESM was trained on
  		baseline_proj <- baseline_raster[[covariates]]

  		baseline_pred <- tryCatch({
  			project_esm_to_raster(esm_model, esm_ensemble, baseline_proj)
  		}, error = function(e) {
  			cat("    ✗ Baseline projection failed:", e$message, "\n")
  			return(NULL)
  		})

  		if (!is.null(baseline_pred)) {
  			writeRaster(
  				baseline_pred,
  				file.path(PREDICTION_DIR, "Baseline", paste0(sp_clean, "_baseline.tif")),
  				overwrite = TRUE
  			)
  			cat("    ✓ Baseline saved (",
  			    round(minmax(baseline_pred)[2], 3), "max prob )\n")
  		}


		## ── Monthly predictions ──────────────────────────────────────────
  		monthly_sp_dir <- file.path(PREDICTION_DIR, "Monthly", sp_clean)
  		dir.create(monthly_sp_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

  		purrr::walk(MONTH_ORDER, function(month_label) {
  
  			raster_key <- paste0("Georgia_Covariates_", month_label)
  
  			if (!raster_key %in% names(monthly_rasters)) {
  				cat("    ⚠ Missing raster for:", month_label, "\n")
  				return(invisible())
  			}

			## Subset monthly raster to ESM covariates
			  month_proj <- monthly_rasters[[raster_key]][[covariates]]

  			month_pred <- tryCatch({
  				project_esm_to_raster(esm_model, esm_ensemble, month_proj)
  			}, error = function(e) {
  				cat("    ✗", month_label, "projection failed:", e$message, "\n")
  				return(NULL)
  			})

  			if (!is.null(month_pred)) {
  				writeRaster(
  					month_pred,
  					file.path(monthly_sp_dir,
  					          paste0(sp_clean, "_", month_label, ".tif")),
  					overwrite = TRUE
  				)
  				cat("    ✓", month_label, "\n")
  			}
  		})

		## Free memory
  		rm(esm_objs, esm_model, esm_ensemble, baseline_proj, baseline_pred)
  		gc()

  		elapsed <- round(difftime(Sys.time(), sp_start, units = "mins"), 1)
  		cat("  Done (", elapsed, "min )\n\n")
  	})
```

```{r Model Evaluation and Landscape Summaries}
# HELPER FUNCTIONS

	#' Extract per-iteration evaluation metrics from a single gbm.step model
	#' Returns CV AUC, training AUC, deviance explained, TSS, and n_presences
  	extract_brt_metrics <- function(model) {
  
  		if (is.null(model)) {
  			return(tibble(
  				cv_auc             = NA_real_,
  				training_auc       = NA_real_,
  				deviance_explained = NA_real_,
  				tss                = NA_real_,
  				n_presences        = NA_integer_
  			))
  		}

		## Training predictions and observed response
		  preds <- model$fitted
		  obs   <- model$gbm.call$dataframe[[model$gbm.call$gbm.y]]

		## dismo evaluation object for TSS computation
  		eval_obj <- tryCatch(
  			dismo::evaluate(p = preds[obs == 1], a = preds[obs == 0]),
  			error = function(e) NULL
  		)

		## TSS = max(sensitivity + specificity - 1) across all thresholds
  		tss_val <- if (!is.null(eval_obj)) {
  			max(eval_obj@TPR + eval_obj@TNR - 1, na.rm = TRUE)
  		} else NA_real_

		## gbm.step internal performance metrics
  		cv_auc  <- model$cv.statistics$discrimination.mean
  		tr_auc  <- model$self.statistics$discrimination
  		dev_exp <- (1 - (model$cv.statistics$deviance.mean /
  		                 model$self.statistics$mean.null)) * 100
  
  		tibble(
  			cv_auc             = cv_auc,
  			training_auc       = tr_auc,
  			deviance_explained = dev_exp,
  			tss                = tss_val,
  			n_presences        = as.integer(sum(obs == 1))
  		)
  	}


	#' Process all 100 BRT models for one species: extract per-iteration
	#' metrics and return summary statistics (mean ± SD)
	#' Boyce index is computed separately from ensemble rasters (see below)
  	summarise_brt_species <- function(sp_name, model_list, tier) {
  
  		cat("  Extracting metrics from", sum(!map_lgl(model_list, is.null)),
  		    "models...\n")
  
  		## Extract metrics from each iteration
    		iter_metrics <- model_list |>
    			map_dfr(extract_brt_metrics)
  
  		## Summarise across iterations
  		tibble(
  			species                 = sp_name,
  			modeling_tier           = tier,
  			n_occurrences           = iter_metrics$n_presences[1],
  			cv_auc_mean             = mean(iter_metrics$cv_auc, na.rm = TRUE),
  			cv_auc_sd               = sd(iter_metrics$cv_auc, na.rm = TRUE),
  			training_auc_mean       = mean(iter_metrics$training_auc, na.rm = TRUE),
  			training_auc_sd         = sd(iter_metrics$training_auc, na.rm = TRUE),
  			deviance_explained_mean = mean(iter_metrics$deviance_explained, na.rm = TRUE),
  			deviance_explained_sd   = sd(iter_metrics$deviance_explained, na.rm = TRUE),
  			tss_mean                = mean(iter_metrics$tss, na.rm = TRUE),
  			tss_sd                  = sd(iter_metrics$tss, na.rm = TRUE),
  			boyce_mean              = NA_real_,
  			boyce_sd                = NA_real_
  		)
  	}


	#' Compute Boyce index for a BRT species using the ensemble mean raster
	#' and occurrence coordinates extracted from the master PA dataset
	#' Returns a single Boyce correlation value (Spearman cor of P/E ratio)
  	compute_brt_boyce <- function(sp_name, pres_coords_sf, baseline_dir) {
  
  		sp_clean <- gsub(" ", "_", sp_name)
  
  		## Load baseline ensemble mean raster
  		baseline_path <- file.path(baseline_dir, paste0(sp_clean, "_baseline.tif"))
  		if (!file.exists(baseline_path)) {
  			cat("    ⚠ Baseline raster not found\n")
  			return(NA_real_)
  		}
  
  		pred_rast <- rast(baseline_path)
  		mean_rast <- if (nlyr(pred_rast) >= 2) pred_rast[[1]] else pred_rast
  
  		## Full landscape predicted values (background distribution)
  		fit_vals <- values(mean_rast, na.rm = TRUE) |> as.numeric()
  
  		## Convert presence coords to SpatVector for extraction
  		pres_vect <- vect(pres_coords_sf)
  
  		## Extract ensemble predictions at known occurrence locations
  		obs_vals <- terra::extract(mean_rast, pres_vect)[[2]] |>
  			na.omit() |>
  			as.numeric()
  
  		if (length(obs_vals) < 5) {
  			cat("    ⚠ Too few valid presence extractions for Boyce\n")
  			return(NA_real_)
  		}
  
  		## Boyce index (predicted-to-expected ratio correlation)
  		boyce_result <- tryCatch(
  			ecospat::ecospat.boyce(
  				fit     = fit_vals,
  				obs     = obs_vals,
  				PEplot  = FALSE
  			),
  			error = function(e) {
  				cat("    ⚠ Boyce computation failed:", e$message, "\n")
  				NULL
  			}
  		)
  
  		if (!is.null(boyce_result)) boyce_result$cor else NA_real_
  	}


	#' Extract evaluation metrics from a saved ESM model object
	#' ESMs store AUC, TSS, and Boyce in the ensemble evaluation output
  	summarise_esm_species <- function(sp_name, esm_objs) {
  
  		esm_ensemble <- esm_objs$esm_ensemble
  
  		## Evaluation metrics from ecospat ensemble
  		evals <- esm_ensemble$ESM.evaluations
  
  		auc_vals   <- evals$AUC
  		tss_vals   <- evals$TSS
  		boyce_vals <- evals$Boyce
  
  		## Attempt to extract n_occurrences from ESM model objects
  		## The BIOMOD formatted data stores presence count; exact accessor
  		## depends on your ESM object structure — adjust as needed
  		n_occ <- tryCatch({
  			if (!is.null(esm_objs$n_presences)) {
  				as.integer(esm_objs$n_presences)
  			} else if (!is.null(esm_objs$biomod_data)) {
  				## biomod2 formatted data stores coords for presences
  				sum(esm_objs$biomod_data@data.species == 1, na.rm = TRUE)
  			} else {
  				NA_integer_
  			}
  		}, error = function(e) NA_integer_)
  
  		tibble(
  			species                 = sp_name,
  			modeling_tier           = "ESM",
  			n_occurrences           = n_occ,
  			cv_auc_mean             = mean(auc_vals, na.rm = TRUE),
  			cv_auc_sd               = sd(auc_vals, na.rm = TRUE),
  			training_auc_mean       = NA_real_,
  			training_auc_sd         = NA_real_,
  			deviance_explained_mean = NA_real_,
  			deviance_explained_sd   = NA_real_,
  			tss_mean                = mean(tss_vals, na.rm = TRUE),
  			tss_sd                  = sd(tss_vals, na.rm = TRUE),
  			boyce_mean              = mean(boyce_vals, na.rm = TRUE),
  			boyce_sd                = sd(boyce_vals, na.rm = TRUE)
  		)
  	}


# PART 1: EXTRACT EVALUATION METRICS

	sdm_extracted <- readRDS(SDM_EXTRACTED_PATH)

	brt_presence_coords <- sdm_extracted |>
		purrr::pmap(function(scientific_name, extracted_sets, ...) {

			## Pull the first iteration's data frame
			  first_set <- extracted_sets[[1]]

	## Compute Boyce for each BRT species and join back to summaries
  	ALL_BRT_SPECIES <- c(STANDARD_BRT_SPECIES, TUNED_BRT_SPECIES)
  
  	brt_boyce_values <- purrr::map_dbl(ALL_BRT_SPECIES, function(sp) {
  
  		cat("  ", sp, "...")
  
  		## Look up presence coordinates for this species
    		if (!sp %in% names(brt_presence_coords)) {
    			cat(" ⚠ Not found in sdm_extracted — check SDM_EXTRACTED_PATH\n")
    			return(NA_real_)
    		}
    
    		boyce_val <- compute_brt_boyce(
    			sp_name      = sp,
    			pres_coords_sf = brt_presence_coords[[sp]],
    			baseline_dir = BASELINE_DIR
    		)
  
    		cat(" Boyce:", round(boyce_val, 3), "\n")
    		boyce_val
    	}) |>
    		set_names(ALL_BRT_SPECIES)
  
  	## Update BRT summaries with Boyce values (SD remains NA — single estimate)
    	standard_brt_summary <- standard_brt_summary |>
    		mutate(
    			boyce_mean = brt_boyce_values[species]
    		)
  
    	tuned_brt_summary <- tuned_brt_summary |>
    		mutate(
    			boyce_mean = brt_boyce_values[species]
    		)
  
  	## Clean up the large PA dataset
  	  rm(sdm_extracted, brt_presence_coords); gc()

	esm_summary <- purrr::map_dfr(ESM_SPECIES, function(sp) {

		sp_clean <- gsub(" ", "_", sp)
		cat(sp, "\n")

		model_path <- file.path(ESM_MODEL_DIR, sp_clean, "esm_model_objects.rds")

		if (!file.exists(model_path)) {
			cat("  ⚠ Model file not found, skipping\n")
			return(tibble(
				species = sp, modeling_tier = "ESM",
				n_occurrences = NA_integer_,
				cv_auc_mean = NA, cv_auc_sd = NA,
				training_auc_mean = NA, training_auc_sd = NA,
				deviance_explained_mean = NA, deviance_explained_sd = NA,
				tss_mean = NA, tss_sd = NA,
				boyce_mean = NA, boyce_sd = NA
			))
		}

		esm_objs <- readRDS(model_path)
		result   <- summarise_esm_species(sp, esm_objs)

		cat("  AUC:", round(result$cv_auc_mean, 3),
		    " | TSS:", round(result$tss_mean, 3),
		    " | Boyce:", round(result$boyce_mean, 3), "\n")

		rm(esm_objs); gc()
		return(result)
	})

	model_evaluation_summary <- bind_rows(
		standard_brt_summary,
		tuned_brt_summary,
		esm_summary
	) |>
		arrange(modeling_tier, species)

	print(model_evaluation_summary, n = 20, width = Inf)

	## Save to CSV
  	write_csv(
  		model_evaluation_summary,
  		file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "model_evaluation_summary.csv")
  	)


	national_summary <- purrr::map_dfr(ALL_SPECIES, function(sp) {

		sp_clean <- gsub(" ", "_", sp)

		## Load baseline prediction raster
		  baseline_path <- file.path(BASELINE_DIR, paste0(sp_clean, "_baseline.tif"))

  		if (!file.exists(baseline_path)) {
  			cat("  ⚠", sp, "— baseline raster not found, skipping\n")
  			return(tibble(species = sp, national_mean = NA, national_sd = NA))
  		}

		pred_rast <- rast(baseline_path)

		## For BRT species, predictions are 2-layer (mean, sd); use the mean layer
		## For ESM species, predictions are 1-layer (mean)
  		mean_rast <- if (nlyr(pred_rast) >= 2) pred_rast[[1]] else pred_rast
  
  		## Extract all non-NA values
  		vals <- values(mean_rast, na.rm = TRUE)
  
  		## National-level summary statistics
  		nat_mean <- mean(vals, na.rm = TRUE)
  		nat_sd   <- sd(vals, na.rm = TRUE)
  
  		cat(sprintf("  %-30s  mean: %.4f  sd: %.4f\n", sp, nat_mean, nat_sd))
  
  		tibble(
  			species       = sp,
  			national_mean = round(nat_mean, 5),
  			national_sd   = round(nat_sd, 5)
  		)
  	})
  
  	print(national_summary, n = 20, width = Inf)

# PART 3: MUNICIPAL-LEVEL SUMMARIES

	## Convert SpatVector to sf for exactextractr compatibility
	  georgia_sf <- st_as_sf(Georgia_adm2)

  	municipal_summary <- purrr::map_dfr(ALL_SPECIES, function(sp) {
  
  		sp_clean <- gsub(" ", "_", sp)
  		cat("  Processing:", sp, "...")
  
  		baseline_path <- file.path(BASELINE_DIR, paste0(sp_clean, "_baseline.tif"))
  
  		if (!file.exists(baseline_path)) {
  			cat(" ⚠ not found\n")
  			return(tibble(
  				species = sp, NAME_2 = georgia_sf$NAME_2,
  				GID_2 = georgia_sf$GID_2,
  				municipal_mean = NA, municipal_sd = NA
  			))
  		}
  
  		pred_rast <- rast(baseline_path)

		## Use the mean prediction layer
		  mean_rast <- if (nlyr(pred_rast) >= 2) pred_rast[[1]] else pred_rast

		## Area-weighted mean suitability per municipality
		  muni_mean <- exact_extract(mean_rast, georgia_sf, fun = "mean")

		## Area-weighted standard deviation per municipality
		  muni_sd <- exact_extract(mean_rast, georgia_sf, fun = "stdev")

  		
  		tibble(
  			species        = sp,
  			NAME_2         = georgia_sf$NAME_2,
  			GID_2          = georgia_sf$GID_2,
  			municipal_mean = round(muni_mean, 5),
  			municipal_sd   = round(muni_sd, 5)
  		)
  	})

  	cat("\n  Municipal summary rows:", nrow(municipal_summary), "\n")
  	cat("  Species × Municipalities:",
  	    n_distinct(municipal_summary$species), "×",
  	    n_distinct(municipal_summary$NAME_2), "\n")


# PART 4: SAVE ALL OUTPUTS

	## Model evaluation summary (performance metrics for all species)
  	write_csv(
  		model_evaluation_summary,
  		file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "model_evaluation_summary.csv")
  	)
  	cat("  ✓ model_evaluation_summary.csv\n")

	## National landscape summary
  	write_csv(
  		national_summary,
  		file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "national_landscape_summary.csv")
  	)
  	cat("  ✓ national_landscape_summary.csv\n")

	## Municipal-level summary (long format: one row per species × municipality)
  	write_csv(
  		municipal_summary,
  		file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "municipal_baseline_summary.csv")
  	)
  	cat("  ✓ municipal_baseline_summary.csv\n")

	## Wide-format version for easier cross-species comparison
	## One row per municipality, columns for each species' mean suitability
  	municipal_wide <- municipal_summary |>
  		dplyr::select(species, NAME_2, GID_2, municipal_mean) |>
  		pivot_wider(
  			names_from  = species,
  			values_from = municipal_mean,
  			names_prefix = "suit_"
  		)

	write_csv(
		municipal_wide,
		file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "municipal_baseline_summary_wide.csv")
	)
	cat("  ✓ municipal_baseline_summary_wide.csv\n")

	cat("\nAll outputs saved to:", OUTPUT_DIR, "\n")
```

```{r Species Distribution Maps — Baseline Mean Suitability}
                                                linewidth = 0.5),

            )
    }
  
  # Reassemble with corrected groupings
    mosquito_figure <- .build_facet_panel(mosquito_long, strip_fill = "#e6f2ff")
    tick_figure     <- .build_facet_panel(tick_long,     strip_fill = "#e6ffe6")

                device   = "svg",
                width    = 14,
                height   = ceiling(n_panels / 4) * 4.5,
                units    = "in"
            )
        }
    )
```

```{r maxSSS Thresholds and Landscape Proportion}

  set.seed(1999)

  # CONFIGURATION

    ## Paths (consistent with prior chunks)
      ONEDRIVE     <- "C:/Users/ianpsheasmith/OneDrive - University of Florida/General - Georgia Ticks/Georgia_Ticks"
      BASELINE_DIR <- file.path(ONEDRIVE, "Paper2_Data/Predictions/Baseline")
      OUTPUT_DIR   <- file.path(ONEDRIVE, "Paper2_Data/Summaries")
      dir.create(OUTPUT_DIR, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

    ## Model directories
      STANDARD_BRT_MODEL_DIR <- file.path(ONEDRIVE, "Paper2_Data/Predictions/Models")
      TUNED_BRT_MODEL_DIR    <- file.path(ONEDRIVE, "Paper2_BRTs_New/Tuned_BRT_Results/models")
      ESM_MODEL_DIR          <- file.path(ONEDRIVE, "Paper2_ESMs")

    ## Species by tier
      STANDARD_BRT_SPECIES <- c(
        "Culex pipiens", "Ixodes ricinus", "Aedes albopictus",
        "Dermacentor marginatus", "Dermacentor reticulatus", "Aedes caspius"
      )

      TUNED_BRT_SPECIES <- c(
        "Aedes vexans", "Culex theileri",
        "Haemaphysalis inermis", "Hyalomma marginatum"
      )

      ESM_SPECIES <- c(
        "Aedes aegypti", "Aedes geniculatus",
        "Anopheles maculipennis", "Anopheles plumbeus", "Anopheles sacharovi",
        "Culex tritaeniorhynchus", "Culiseta annulata", "Culiseta longiareolata",
        "Hyalomma aegyptium", "Rhipicephalus sanguineus"
      )


  # maxSSS COMPUTATION

    #' Compute the maxSSS threshold from a vector of predictions and binary observed values
    #' Evaluates candidate thresholds and returns the value maximising sensitivity + specificity
      compute_maxsss <- function(preds, obs) {

        pres_p <- preds[obs == 1]
        abs_p  <- preds[obs == 0]

        ## Generate candidate thresholds from the unique predicted values
          cands <- sort(unique(preds[!is.na(preds)]))

        ## Downsample candidates if the set is very large (speed optimisation)
          if (length(cands) > 500) {
            cands <- quantile(cands, seq(0, 1, length.out = 500), na.rm = TRUE)
          }

        ## Evaluate sensitivity + specificity at each candidate
          ss <- purrr::map_dbl(cands, function(t) {
            sum(pres_p >= t) / length(pres_p) + sum(abs_p < t) / length(abs_p)
          })

        cands[which.max(ss)]
      }


    #' Extract maxSSS from a single fitted gbm.step model object
    #' Uses the training fitted values and observed response stored in the model
      extract_brt_maxsss <- function(model) {

        if (is.null(model)) return(NA_real_)

        ## Recover fitted predictions and observed binary response
          preds <- model$fitted
          obs   <- model$gbm.call$dataframe[[model$gbm.call$gbm.y]]

        compute_maxsss(preds, obs)
      }


  # PART 1: BRT THRESHOLDS (Standard + Tuned)
  ## For each species, load the 100 saved model objects, compute maxSSS per
  ## iteration, and summarise as mean ± SD across the ensemble

    brt_threshold_specs <- bind_rows(
      tibble(
        species    = STANDARD_BRT_SPECIES,
        tier       = "Standard_BRT",
        model_dir  = STANDARD_BRT_MODEL_DIR,
        file_suffix = "_models.rds"
      ),
      tibble(
        species    = TUNED_BRT_SPECIES,
        tier       = "Tuned_BRT",
        model_dir  = TUNED_BRT_MODEL_DIR,
        file_suffix = "_tuned_brt_models.rds"
      )
    )

    brt_thresholds <- purrr::pmap_dfr(brt_threshold_specs, function(species, tier, model_dir, file_suffix) {

      sp_clean   <- gsub(" ", "_", species)
      model_path <- file.path(model_dir, paste0(sp_clean, file_suffix))

      cat(species, "(", tier, ") ...")

      if (!file.exists(model_path)) {
        cat(" ⚠ model file not found\n")
        return(tibble(
          species       = species,
          modeling_tier = tier,
          maxsss_mean   = NA_real_,
          maxsss_sd     = NA_real_,
          n_models      = NA_integer_
        ))
      }

      ## Load the list of 100 gbm.step model objects
        models <- readRDS(model_path)

      ## Compute maxSSS from each valid iteration
        iter_thresholds <- purrr::map_dbl(models, extract_brt_maxsss)

      ## Remove NAs from failed iterations
        valid_thresholds <- iter_thresholds[!is.na(iter_thresholds)]

      cat(" ", length(valid_thresholds), "valid |",
          "maxSSS:", round(mean(valid_thresholds), 4), "±",
          round(sd(valid_thresholds), 4), "\n")

      rm(models); gc()

      tibble(
        species       = species,
        modeling_tier = tier,
        maxsss_mean   = mean(valid_thresholds),
        maxsss_sd     = sd(valid_thresholds),
        n_models      = length(valid_thresholds)
      )
    })


  # PART 2: ESM THRESHOLDS
  ## These were already computed and saved during the ESM fitting pipeline;
  ## retrieve them from the stored model objects

    esm_thresholds <- purrr::map_dfr(ESM_SPECIES, function(sp) {

      sp_clean   <- gsub(" ", "_", sp)
      model_path <- file.path(ESM_MODEL_DIR, sp_clean, "esm_model_objects.rds")

      cat(sp, "(ESM) ...")

      if (!file.exists(model_path)) {
        cat(" ⚠ model file not found\n")
        return(tibble(
          species       = sp,
          modeling_tier = "ESM",
          maxsss_mean   = NA_real_,
          maxsss_sd     = NA_real_,
          n_models      = NA_integer_
        ))
      }

      esm_objs <- readRDS(model_path)

      ## ESM pipeline saved a single maxSSS value (no per-iteration SD available)
        maxsss_val <- esm_objs$thresholds$maxsss

      cat(" maxSSS:", round(maxsss_val, 4), "\n")

      tibble(
        species       = sp,
        modeling_tier = "ESM",
        maxsss_mean   = maxsss_val,
        maxsss_sd     = NA_real_,
        n_models      = 1L
      )
    })


  # COMBINE ALL THRESHOLDS

    all_thresholds <- bind_rows(brt_thresholds, esm_thresholds) |>
      arrange(modeling_tier, species)

    cat("\n══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n")
    cat("  maxSSS THRESHOLDS — ALL SPECIES\n")
    cat("══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n\n")
    print(all_thresholds, n = 20, width = Inf)


  # PART 3: BINARY CLASSIFICATION + LANDSCAPE PROPORTION
  ## Apply each species' mean maxSSS threshold to the baseline prediction raster
  ## to classify every pixel as present (≥ threshold) or absent (< threshold),
  ## then compute the proportion of the landscape classified as present

    landscape_proportion <- purrr::pmap_dfr(all_thresholds, function(species, modeling_tier,
                                                                       maxsss_mean, maxsss_sd,
                                                                       n_models) {

      sp_clean      <- gsub(" ", "_", species)
      baseline_path <- file.path(BASELINE_DIR, paste0(sp_clean, "_baseline.tif"))

      cat("  ", species, "...")

      if (is.na(maxsss_mean) || !file.exists(baseline_path)) {
        cat(" ⚠ skipped (missing threshold or raster)\n")
        return(tibble(
          species            = species,
          modeling_tier      = modeling_tier,
          maxsss_threshold   = maxsss_mean,
          n_pixels_total     = NA_integer_,
          n_pixels_present   = NA_integer_,
          pct_landscape      = NA_real_
        ))
      }

      ## Load baseline raster (BRT = 2-layer [mean, sd]; ESM = 1-layer)
        pred_rast <- rast(baseline_path)
        mean_rast <- if (nlyr(pred_rast) >= 2) pred_rast[[1]] else pred_rast

      ## Binary classification: 1 if predicted probability ≥ threshold, else 0
        binary_rast <- mean_rast >= maxsss_mean

      ## Extract pixel counts (non-NA cells only)
        all_vals     <- values(binary_rast, na.rm = TRUE)
        n_total      <- length(all_vals)
        n_present    <- sum(all_vals == 1)
        pct_present  <- (n_present / n_total) * 100

      cat(" ", round(pct_present, 2), "% present\n")

      tibble(
        species            = species,
        modeling_tier      = modeling_tier,
        maxsss_threshold   = round(maxsss_mean, 4),
        n_pixels_total     = as.integer(n_total),
        n_pixels_present   = as.integer(n_present),
        pct_landscape      = round(pct_present, 2)
      )
    })


  # RESULTS

    cat("\n══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n")
    cat("  LANDSCAPE PROPORTION AT maxSSS — ALL SPECIES\n")
    cat("══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n\n")
    print(landscape_proportion, n = 20, width = Inf)


  # OPTIONAL: SAVE BINARY RASTERS
  ## Writes a classified present/absent .tif for each species alongside the
  ## continuous baseline predictions

    BINARY_DIR <- file.path(ONEDRIVE, "Paper2_Data/Predictions/Binary_maxSSS")
    dir.create(BINARY_DIR, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

    purrr::pwalk(
      landscape_proportion |> dplyr::filter(!is.na(maxsss_threshold)),
      function(species, modeling_tier, maxsss_threshold, ...) {

        sp_clean      <- gsub(" ", "_", species)
        baseline_path <- file.path(BASELINE_DIR, paste0(sp_clean, "_baseline.tif"))

        pred_rast   <- rast(baseline_path)
        mean_rast   <- if (nlyr(pred_rast) >= 2) pred_rast[[1]] else pred_rast
        binary_rast <- mean_rast >= maxsss_threshold

        names(binary_rast) <- "present"

        writeRaster(
          binary_rast,
          file.path(BINARY_DIR, paste0(sp_clean, "_binary_maxsss.tif")),
          overwrite = TRUE,
          datatype  = "INT1U"
        )
      }
    )

    cat("\nBinary rasters saved to:\n ", BINARY_DIR, "\n")


  # SAVE SUMMARY TABLES

    ## Thresholds table
      write_csv(
        all_thresholds,
        file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "maxsss_thresholds_all_species.csv")
      )

    ## Landscape proportion table
      write_csv(
        landscape_proportion,
        file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "landscape_proportion_at_maxsss.csv")
      )

    ## Combined table (merge thresholds with landscape stats)
      combined_summary <- all_thresholds |>
        left_join(
          landscape_proportion |> dplyr::select(species, n_pixels_total, n_pixels_present, pct_landscape),
          by = "species"
        )

      write_csv(
        combined_summary,
        file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "maxsss_threshold_and_landscape_summary.csv")
      )

    cat("\nSummary tables saved to:\n ", OUTPUT_DIR, "\n")
```

```{r Vector Groupings Construction w/ Monte Carlo for maxSSS}
## ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
## DISEASE RISK INDEX CONSTRUCTION — MONTE CARLO UNCERTAINTY PROPAGATION
##
## Constructs municipality-level pathogen-vector group exposure indices by:
##   1. Classifying municipal suitability against species-specific maxSSS thresholds
##   2. Weighting binary indicators by literature-derived vector competence weights
##   3. Propagating uncertainty through 1,000 Monte Carlo iterations
##      (sampling both weights and thresholds from truncated normal distributions)
##
## Inputs:
##   - Municipal baseline summary (species × municipality mean suitability)
##   - maxSSS thresholds (species-level mean ± SD from 100 BRT/ESM models)
##   - Vector competence weight specifications (central + lower/upper bounds)
##
## Outputs:
##   - Municipality-level disease group exposure indices with credible intervals
##   - Summary CSV for downstream INFORM-style risk index construction
## ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════




set.seed(1999)


# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# CONFIGURATION
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

	ONEDRIVE   <- "C:/Users/ianpsheasmith/OneDrive - University of Florida/General - Georgia Ticks/Georgia_Ticks"
	OUTPUT_DIR <- file.path(ONEDRIVE, "Paper2_Data/Summaries")
	dir.create(OUTPUT_DIR, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

	## Input files (produced by earlier chunks)
	MUNICIPAL_SUIT_PATH <- file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "municipal_baseline_summary.csv")
	THRESHOLD_PATH      <- file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "maxsss_thresholds_all_species.csv")

	## Monte Carlo parameters
	N_ITERATIONS <- 1000
	SEED         <- 1999

	## Climate scenarios to process
	## For now, baseline only — extend to warming scenarios by providing
	## additional municipal summary files keyed by scenario
	SCENARIOS <- c("Baseline")


# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# DISEASE GROUP WEIGHT SPECIFICATIONS
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
## Raw weights and bounds derived from the vector competence literature review.
## Bounds are interpreted as approximate 95% credible intervals for
## parameterising truncated normal distributions during Monte Carlo sampling.
## Weights are renormalised to sum to unity within each group at each iteration.

	disease_weights <- tribble(
		~disease_group,    ~species,                    ~weight_raw, ~weight_lower, ~weight_upper,

		## Emerging Aedes-borne Viruses (CHIKV / DENV / ZIKV)
		"aedes_arbo",      "Aedes aegypti",              1.00,        0.90,          1.00,
		"aedes_arbo",      "Aedes albopictus",           0.90,        0.80,          1.00,
		"aedes_arbo",      "Aedes geniculatus",          0.15,        0.05,          0.25,
		"aedes_arbo",      "Aedes vexans",               0.05,        0.01,          0.10,

		## West Nile Virus Complex (WNV / USUV / SINV)
		"wnv_complex",     "Culex pipiens",              1.00,        0.90,          1.00,
		"wnv_complex",     "Culex theileri",             0.50,        0.30,          0.70,
		"wnv_complex",     "Culex tritaeniorhynchus",    0.40,        0.20,          0.60,
		"wnv_complex",     "Aedes vexans",               0.15,        0.05,          0.25,
		"wnv_complex",     "Culiseta annulata",          0.15,        0.05,          0.25,

		## Malaria (Plasmodium falciparum / P. vivax)
		"malaria",         "Anopheles sacharovi",        1.00,        0.90,          1.00,
		"malaria",         "Anopheles maculipennis",     0.50,        0.30,          0.70,
		"malaria",         "Anopheles plumbeus",         0.50,        0.30,          0.70,

		## Tick-borne Encephalitis Virus (TBEV)
		"tbe",             "Ixodes ricinus",             1.00,        0.90,          1.00,
		"tbe",             "Dermacentor reticulatus",    0.40,        0.20,          0.60,
		"tbe",             "Haemaphysalis inermis",      0.30,        0.15,          0.45,
		"tbe",             "Dermacentor marginatus",     0.15,        0.05,          0.25,

		## Lyme Borreliosis (Borrelia burgdorferi s.l.)
		"lyme",            "Ixodes ricinus",             1.00,        0.95,          1.00,

		## Spotted Fever Group Rickettsioses
		"sfg_rickettsia",  "Rhipicephalus sanguineus",   1.00,        0.85,          1.00,
		"sfg_rickettsia",  "Dermacentor marginatus",     0.85,        0.70,          1.00,
		"sfg_rickettsia",  "Dermacentor reticulatus",    0.70,        0.50,          0.90,
		"sfg_rickettsia",  "Hyalomma marginatum",        0.65,        0.45,          0.85,
		"sfg_rickettsia",  "Hyalomma aegyptium",         0.05,        0.01,          0.10,

		## Crimean-Congo Haemorrhagic Fever Virus (CCHFV)
		"cchf",            "Hyalomma marginatum",        1.00,        0.90,          1.00,
		"cchf",            "Hyalomma aegyptium",         0.25,        0.10,          0.40,

		## Tularaemia (Francisella tularensis)
		"tularemia",       "Dermacentor marginatus",     1.00,        0.90,          1.00,
		"tularemia",       "Ixodes ricinus",             0.25,        0.10,          0.40,
		"tularemia",       "Dermacentor reticulatus",    0.25,        0.10,          0.40
	)

	## Readable labels for output and plotting
	disease_labels <- tribble(
		~disease_group,    ~disease_label,
		"aedes_arbo",      "Emerging Aedes-borne Viruses",
		"wnv_complex",     "West Nile Virus Complex",
		"malaria",         "Malaria (Receptivity)",
		"tbe",             "Tick-borne Encephalitis",
		"lyme",            "Lyme Borreliosis",
		"sfg_rickettsia",  "Spotted Fever Rickettsioses",
		"cchf",            "Crimean-Congo Haemorrhagic Fever",
		"tularemia",       "Tularaemia"
	)


# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# LOAD INPUT DATA
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

	## Municipal suitability: long format (species × municipality)
	municipal_suit <- read_csv(MUNICIPAL_SUIT_PATH, show_col_types = FALSE)

	## maxSSS thresholds: species-level mean ± SD from the 100-iteration ensemble
	thresholds <- read_csv(THRESHOLD_PATH, show_col_types = FALSE)

	## Verify species alignment between weights and available data
	available_species <- unique(municipal_suit$species)
	required_species  <- unique(disease_weights$species)

	missing_species <- setdiff(required_species, available_species)
	if (length(missing_species) > 0) {
		warning(
			"Species in weight table not found in municipal suitability data:\n  ",
			paste(missing_species, collapse = "\n  "),
			"\n  These will be excluded from their disease groups."
		)
	}

	## Filter weights to available species only
	disease_weights <- disease_weights |>
		dplyr::filter(species %in% available_species)

	## Verify threshold availability
	threshold_species <- unique(thresholds$species)
	missing_thresholds <- setdiff(
		unique(disease_weights$species),
		threshold_species
	)

	if (length(missing_thresholds) > 0) {
		warning(
			"Species missing from thresholds table:\n  ",
			paste(missing_thresholds, collapse = "\n  ")
		)
	}

	## Municipalities
	municipalities <- municipal_suit |>
		dplyr::select(NAME_2, GID_2) |>
		distinct()

	n_municipalities <- nrow(municipalities)
	disease_groups   <- unique(disease_weights$disease_group)
	n_groups         <- length(disease_groups)

	cat("══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n")
	cat("  MONTE CARLO DISEASE RISK INDEX CONSTRUCTION\n")
	cat("══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n\n")
	cat("  Municipalities:    ", n_municipalities, "\n")
	cat("  Disease groups:    ", n_groups, "\n")
	cat("  Species modelled:  ", length(unique(disease_weights$species)), "\n")
	cat("  MC iterations:     ", N_ITERATIONS, "\n\n")


# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# HELPER FUNCTIONS
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

	#' Estimate SD from lower/upper bounds interpreted as ~95% CI
	#' For a normal distribution, 95% CI spans ±1.96 SD,
	#' so the range covers ~3.92 SDs
	bounds_to_sd <- function(lower, upper) {
		(upper - lower) / 3.92
	}

	#' Pre-compute truncated normal samples for a single weight specification
	#' Returns a numeric vector of length n_samples
	sample_weight <- function(central, lower, upper, n_samples) {
		sd_est <- bounds_to_sd(lower, upper)
		truncnorm::rtruncnorm(
			n    = n_samples,
			a    = 0,
			b    = 1,
			mean = central,
			sd   = sd_est
		)
	}

	#' Pre-compute truncated normal samples for a threshold specification
	#' Uses the empirical mean ± SD from the 100 BRT model ensemble
	sample_threshold <- function(threshold_mean, threshold_sd, n_samples) {

		## ESM species may have NA SD (single threshold); treat as fixed
		if (is.na(threshold_sd) || threshold_sd == 0) {
			return(rep(threshold_mean, n_samples))
		}

		truncnorm::rtruncnorm(
			n    = n_samples,
			a    = 0,
			b    = 1,
			mean = threshold_mean,
			sd   = threshold_sd
		)
	}


# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# PRE-SAMPLE ALL STOCHASTIC INPUTS
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
## Pre-sampling once avoids repeated RNG calls inside the iteration loop
## and ensures full reproducibility from a single seed

	set.seed(SEED)

	cat("Pre-sampling weight distributions...\n")

	## Weight samples: named list of numeric vectors (length = N_ITERATIONS)
	## Keyed by paste(disease_group, species)
	weight_samples <- disease_weights |>
		mutate(
			sample_key = paste(disease_group, species, sep = "::"),
			samples    = pmap(
				list(weight_raw, weight_lower, weight_upper),
				~ sample_weight(..1, ..2, ..3, N_ITERATIONS)
			)
		) |>
		dplyr::select(sample_key, samples) |>
		deframe()

	cat("Pre-sampling threshold distributions...\n")

	## Threshold samples: named list of numeric vectors (length = N_ITERATIONS)
	## Keyed by species name
	threshold_samples <- thresholds |>
		dplyr::filter(species %in% unique(disease_weights$species)) |>
		mutate(
			samples = pmap(
				list(maxsss_mean, maxsss_sd),
				~ sample_threshold(..1, ..2, N_ITERATIONS)
			)
		) |>
		dplyr::select(species, samples) |>
		deframe()

	cat("  Weight sample keys:    ", length(weight_samples), "\n")
	cat("  Threshold sample keys: ", length(threshold_samples), "\n\n")


# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# BUILD MUNICIPAL SUITABILITY LOOKUP
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
## Convert to a named list of named vectors for fast lookup:
##   suit_lookup[["species_name"]] → named vector (municipality → mean suitability)

	suit_lookup <- municipal_suit |>
		dplyr::filter(species %in% unique(disease_weights$species)) |>
		dplyr::select(species, NAME_2, municipal_mean) |>
		split(~species) |>
		purrr::map(~ set_names(.x$municipal_mean, .x$NAME_2))

	cat("Built suitability lookup for", length(suit_lookup), "species\n\n")


# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# MONTE CARLO SIMULATION
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
## For each disease group and iteration:
##   1. Retrieve pre-sampled weights → renormalise to sum to 1
##   2. Retrieve pre-sampled thresholds for each species
##   3. Classify each municipality as suitable/unsuitable (binary)
##   4. Compute weighted sum of binary indicators
##
## Results stored as a matrix: rows = municipalities, cols = iterations

	cat("Running Monte Carlo simulation...\n")

	mc_results <- purrr::map(disease_groups, function(dg) {

		cat("  ", dg, "...\n")

		## Species in this disease group
		group_spec <- disease_weights |>
			dplyr::filter(disease_group == dg)

		group_species <- group_spec$species

		## Pre-allocate result matrix (municipalities × iterations)
		result_mat <- matrix(
			NA_real_,
			nrow = n_municipalities,
			ncol = N_ITERATIONS,
			dimnames = list(municipalities$NAME_2, NULL)
		)

		## Run all iterations using vectorised operations
		purrr::walk(seq_len(N_ITERATIONS), function(iter) {

			## Retrieve and renormalise sampled weights for this iteration
			raw_weights <- purrr::map_dbl(group_species, function(sp) {
				key <- paste(dg, sp, sep = "::")
				weight_samples[[key]][iter]
			})
			norm_weights <- raw_weights / sum(raw_weights)

			## For each species: classify municipalities as suitable/unsuitable
			## using the sampled threshold, then apply the normalised weight
			weighted_binary <- purrr::map2_dfc(
				group_species,
				norm_weights,
				function(sp, wt) {

					## Sampled threshold for this species at this iteration
					thresh <- threshold_samples[[sp]][iter]

					## Municipal mean suitability values
					suit_vals <- suit_lookup[[sp]][municipalities$NAME_2]

					## Binary classification: suitable if mean suitability >= threshold
					binary <- as.numeric(suit_vals >= thresh)

					## Weighted contribution
					tibble(!!sp := binary * wt)
				}
			)

			## Sum across species for this iteration's exposure index
			result_mat[, iter] <<- rowSums(weighted_binary, na.rm = TRUE)
		})

		result_mat
	}) |>
		set_names(disease_groups)

	cat("  Monte Carlo simulation complete.\n\n")


# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# SUMMARISE MC RESULTS
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
## For each disease group × municipality, compute:
##   - mean exposure (point estimate)
##   - SD (uncertainty)
##   - 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles (95% credible interval)

	disease_exposure <- purrr::map_dfr(disease_groups, function(dg) {

		mat <- mc_results[[dg]]

		tibble(
			disease_group = dg,
			NAME_2        = municipalities$NAME_2,
			GID_2         = municipalities$GID_2,
			exposure_mean = rowMeans(mat, na.rm = TRUE),
			exposure_sd   = apply(mat, 1, sd, na.rm = TRUE),
			exposure_q025 = apply(mat, 1, quantile, probs = 0.025, na.rm = TRUE),
			exposure_q975 = apply(mat, 1, quantile, probs = 0.975, na.rm = TRUE)
		)
	}) |>
		left_join(disease_labels, by = "disease_group")

	cat("══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n")
	cat("  DISEASE EXPOSURE SUMMARY (Baseline)\n")
	cat("══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n\n")

	## Group-level summary statistics
	disease_exposure |>
		group_by(disease_group, disease_label) |>
		summarise(
			mean_exposure      = round(mean(exposure_mean), 4),
			sd_exposure        = round(mean(exposure_sd), 4),
			min_exposure       = round(min(exposure_mean), 4),
			max_exposure       = round(max(exposure_mean), 4),
			n_municipalities   = n(),
			.groups = "drop"
		) |>
		print(n = 20, width = Inf)


# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# DIAGNOSTICS: WEIGHT SENSITIVITY CHECK
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
## Compute the coefficient of variation (CV) of the Monte Carlo exposure
## estimates as a measure of how sensitive each disease group is to
## weight perturbation. High CV = high sensitivity to weight choices.

	cat("\n\n══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n")
	cat("  WEIGHT SENSITIVITY — COEFFICIENT OF VARIATION\n")
	cat("══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n\n")

	sensitivity_summary <- disease_exposure |>
		mutate(
			cv = if_else(exposure_mean > 0, exposure_sd / exposure_mean, NA_real_)
		) |>
		group_by(disease_group, disease_label) |>
		summarise(
			mean_cv = round(mean(cv, na.rm = TRUE), 4),
			max_cv  = round(max(cv, na.rm = TRUE), 4),
			.groups = "drop"
		) |>
		arrange(desc(mean_cv))

	print(sensitivity_summary, n = 20, width = Inf)

	cat("\n  Interpretation:\n")
	cat("    CV < 0.05 → Minimal sensitivity to weight perturbation\n")
	cat("    CV 0.05–0.15 → Moderate sensitivity\n")
	cat("    CV > 0.15 → High sensitivity — consider tightening evidence bounds\n\n")


# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# SAVE OUTPUTS
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

	## Long format: one row per disease group × municipality
	write_csv(
		disease_exposure,
		file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "disease_exposure_mc_baseline.csv")
	)
	cat("  ✓ disease_exposure_mc_baseline.csv\n")

	## Wide format: one row per municipality, columns per disease group
	disease_exposure_wide <- disease_exposure |>
		dplyr::select(NAME_2, GID_2, disease_group, exposure_mean) |>
		pivot_wider(
			names_from  = disease_group,
			values_from = exposure_mean,
			names_prefix = "exposure_"
		)

	write_csv(
		disease_exposure_wide,
		file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "disease_exposure_mc_baseline_wide.csv")
	)
	cat("  ✓ disease_exposure_mc_baseline_wide.csv\n")

	## Sensitivity summary
	write_csv(
		sensitivity_summary,
		file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "weight_sensitivity_cv.csv")
	)
	cat("  ✓ weight_sensitivity_cv.csv\n")

	cat("\nAll outputs saved to:", OUTPUT_DIR, "\n")
```

```{r Vect. Group Maps w/ maxSSS}
## ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
## DISEASE EXPOSURE INDEX — MUNICIPAL CHOROPLETH MAPS
##
## Joins MC exposure estimates to the ADM2 shapefile and renders one
## choropleth per disease group using a shared viridis fill scale.
## Fixed scale across all facets enables direct cross-group comparison.
## ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

## Join exposure data to spatial object
exposure_sf <- Georgia_adm2_sf |>
    left_join(
        disease_exposure |>
            dplyr::select(GID_2, disease_group, disease_label, exposure_mean),
        by = "GID_2"
    )

## Compute shared scale limits across all disease groups
exposure_range <- range(disease_exposure$exposure_mean, na.rm = TRUE)

## Build the faceted map
ggplot(exposure_sf) +
    geom_sf(
        aes(fill = exposure_mean),
        colour = "white",
        linewidth = 0.15
    ) +
    scale_fill_viridis_c(
        option    = "viridis",
        name      = "Exposure\nIndex",
        limits    = exposure_range,
        na.value  = "grey85",
        guide     = guide_colorbar(
            barwidth  = 0.5,
            barheight = 6,
            ticks     = FALSE
        )
    ) +
    facet_wrap(
        ~ disease_label,
        ncol = 2
    ) +
    labs(
        title    = "Municipal Vector-borne Disease Exposure Indices — Baseline",
        subtitle = "Monte Carlo mean exposure (1,000 iterations) — shared scale across all groups",
        caption  = "Exposure index: weighted sum of binary suitability classifications\nWeights derived from vector competence literature"
    ) +
    theme_void(base_size = 11) +
    theme(
        plot.title       = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13, margin = ggplot2::margin(b = 4)),
        plot.subtitle    = element_text(size = 10, colour = "grey40", margin = ggplot2::margin(b = 10)),
        plot.caption     = element_text(size = 7, colour = "grey55", margin = ggplot2::margin(t = 8)),
        strip.text       = element_text(face = "bold", size = 9, margin = ggplot2::margin(b = 4)),
        legend.position  = "right",
        panel.spacing    = unit(0.8, "lines"),
        plot.margin      = ggplot2::margin(10, 10, 10, 10)
    )
```

```{r Vector Groupings Construction w/ Monte Carlo for simple cont. values}
## ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
## DISEASE RISK INDEX CONSTRUCTION — CONTINUOUS SUITABILITY APPROACH
##
## Constructs municipality-level pathogen-vector group exposure indices using
## continuous habitat suitability values (rather than binary maxSSS thresholds)
## weighted by literature-derived vector competence weights, with uncertainty
## propagated via 1,000 Monte Carlo iterations.
##
## Key difference from the binary approach:
##   Binary:     E = Σ w_i × I(suit_i ≥ threshold_i)
##   Continuous: E = Σ w_i × suit_i
##
## The continuous formulation preserves suitability gradients and eliminates
## threshold boundary artefacts that inflate uncertainty for widespread species
## (e.g., Cx. pipiens) with municipalities near the maxSSS decision boundary.
##
## Inputs:
##   - Municipal baseline summary (species × municipality mean suitability)
##   - Vector competence weight specifications (central + lower/upper bounds)
##
## Outputs:
##   - Municipality-level disease group exposure indices with credible intervals
##   - Comparison diagnostics against the binary approach
## ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

library(tidyverse)
library(truncnorm)

set.seed(1999)


# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# CONFIGURATION
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

	ONEDRIVE   <- "C:/Users/ianpsheasmith/OneDrive - University of Florida/General - Georgia Ticks/Georgia_Ticks"
	OUTPUT_DIR <- file.path(ONEDRIVE, "Paper2_Data/Summaries")
	dir.create(OUTPUT_DIR, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

	## Input file (produced by earlier extraction chunk)
	MUNICIPAL_SUIT_PATH <- file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "municipal_baseline_summary.csv")

	## Monte Carlo parameters
	N_ITERATIONS <- 1000
	SEED         <- 1999


# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# DISEASE GROUP WEIGHT SPECIFICATIONS
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
## Raw weights and bounds from the vector competence literature review.
## Bounds interpreted as approximate 95% credible intervals for truncated
## normal sampling. Weights renormalised to sum to unity within each group
## at each MC iteration.

	disease_weights <- tribble(
		~disease_group,    ~species,                    ~weight_raw, ~weight_lower, ~weight_upper,

		## Emerging Aedes-borne Viruses (CHIKV / DENV / ZIKV)
		"aedes_arbo",      "Aedes aegypti",              1.00,        0.90,          1.00,
		"aedes_arbo",      "Aedes albopictus",           0.90,        0.80,          1.00,
		"aedes_arbo",      "Aedes geniculatus",          0.15,        0.05,          0.25,
		"aedes_arbo",      "Aedes vexans",               0.05,        0.01,          0.10,

		## West Nile Virus Complex (WNV / USUV / SINV)
		"wnv_complex",     "Culex pipiens",              1.00,        0.90,          1.00,
		"wnv_complex",     "Culex theileri",             0.50,        0.30,          0.70,
		"wnv_complex",     "Culex tritaeniorhynchus",    0.40,        0.20,          0.60,
		"wnv_complex",     "Aedes vexans",               0.15,        0.05,          0.25,
		"wnv_complex",     "Culiseta annulata",          0.15,        0.05,          0.25,

		## Malaria (Plasmodium falciparum / P. vivax)
		"malaria",         "Anopheles sacharovi",        1.00,        0.90,          1.00,
		"malaria",         "Anopheles maculipennis",     0.50,        0.30,          0.70,
		"malaria",         "Anopheles plumbeus",         0.50,        0.30,          0.70,

		## Tick-borne Encephalitis Virus (TBEV)
		"tbe",             "Ixodes ricinus",             1.00,        0.90,          1.00,
		"tbe",             "Dermacentor reticulatus",    0.40,        0.20,          0.60,
		"tbe",             "Haemaphysalis inermis",      0.30,        0.15,          0.45,
		"tbe",             "Dermacentor marginatus",     0.15,        0.05,          0.25,

		## Lyme Borreliosis (Borrelia burgdorferi s.l.)
		"lyme",            "Ixodes ricinus",             1.00,        0.95,          1.00,

		## Spotted Fever Group Rickettsioses
		"sfg_rickettsia",  "Rhipicephalus sanguineus",   1.00,        0.85,          1.00,
		"sfg_rickettsia",  "Dermacentor marginatus",     0.85,        0.70,          1.00,
		"sfg_rickettsia",  "Dermacentor reticulatus",    0.70,        0.50,          0.90,
		"sfg_rickettsia",  "Hyalomma marginatum",        0.65,        0.45,          0.85,
		"sfg_rickettsia",  "Hyalomma aegyptium",         0.05,        0.01,          0.10,

		## Crimean-Congo Haemorrhagic Fever Virus (CCHFV)
		"cchf",            "Hyalomma marginatum",        1.00,        0.90,          1.00,
		"cchf",            "Hyalomma aegyptium",         0.25,        0.10,          0.40,

		## Tularaemia (Francisella tularensis)
		"tularemia",       "Dermacentor marginatus",     1.00,        0.90,          1.00,
		"tularemia",       "Ixodes ricinus",             0.25,        0.10,          0.40,
		"tularemia",       "Dermacentor reticulatus",    0.25,        0.10,          0.40
	)

	## Readable labels for output and plotting
	disease_labels <- tribble(
		~disease_group,    ~disease_label,
		"aedes_arbo",      "Emerging Aedes-borne Viruses",
		"wnv_complex",     "West Nile Virus Complex",
		"malaria",         "Malaria (Receptivity)",
		"tbe",             "Tick-borne Encephalitis",
		"lyme",            "Lyme Borreliosis",
		"sfg_rickettsia",  "Spotted Fever Rickettsioses",
		"cchf",            "Crimean-Congo Haemorrhagic Fever",
		"tularemia",       "Tularaemia"
	)


# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# LOAD INPUT DATA
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

	municipal_suit <- read_csv(MUNICIPAL_SUIT_PATH, show_col_types = FALSE)

	## Filter weights to species with available suitability data
	available_species <- unique(municipal_suit$species)
	required_species  <- unique(disease_weights$species)

	missing_species <- setdiff(required_species, available_species)
	if (length(missing_species) > 0) {
		warning(
			"Species in weight table not found in municipal suitability data:\n  ",
			paste(missing_species, collapse = "\n  "),
			"\n  These will be excluded from their disease groups."
		)
	}

	disease_weights <- disease_weights |>
		dplyr::filter(species %in% available_species)

	## Municipality reference table
	municipalities <- municipal_suit |>
		dplyr::select(NAME_2, GID_2) |>
		distinct()

	n_municipalities <- nrow(municipalities)
	disease_groups   <- unique(disease_weights$disease_group)
	n_groups         <- length(disease_groups)

	cat("══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n")
	cat("  CONTINUOUS SUITABILITY — MC DISEASE RISK INDEX\n")
	cat("══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n\n")
	cat("  Municipalities:    ", n_municipalities, "\n")
	cat("  Disease groups:    ", n_groups, "\n")
	cat("  Species modelled:  ", length(unique(disease_weights$species)), "\n")
	cat("  MC iterations:     ", N_ITERATIONS, "\n\n")


# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# HELPER FUNCTIONS
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

	#' Estimate SD from lower/upper bounds interpreted as ~95% CI
	bounds_to_sd <- function(lower, upper) {
		(upper - lower) / 3.92
	}

	#' Sample weights from truncated normal distribution bounded [0, 1]
	sample_weight <- function(central, lower, upper, n_samples) {
		sd_est <- bounds_to_sd(lower, upper)
		truncnorm::rtruncnorm(
			n    = n_samples,
			a    = 0,
			b    = 1,
			mean = central,
			sd   = sd_est
		)
	}


# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# PRE-SAMPLE WEIGHT DISTRIBUTIONS
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

	set.seed(SEED)

	cat("Pre-sampling weight distributions...\n")

	weight_samples <- disease_weights |>
		mutate(
			sample_key = paste(disease_group, species, sep = "::"),
			samples    = pmap(
				list(weight_raw, weight_lower, weight_upper),
				~ sample_weight(..1, ..2, ..3, N_ITERATIONS)
			)
		) |>
		dplyr::select(sample_key, samples) |>
		deframe()

	cat("  Weight sample keys: ", length(weight_samples), "\n\n")


# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# BUILD MUNICIPAL SUITABILITY LOOKUP
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
## Named list of named vectors: suit_lookup[["species"]] → c(muni1 = val, ...)

	suit_lookup <- municipal_suit |>
		dplyr::filter(species %in% unique(disease_weights$species)) |>
		dplyr::select(species, NAME_2, municipal_mean) |>
		split(~species) |>
		purrr::map(~ set_names(.x$municipal_mean, .x$NAME_2))

	cat("Built suitability lookup for", length(suit_lookup), "species\n\n")


# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# MONTE CARLO SIMULATION — CONTINUOUS SUITABILITY
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
## For each disease group and iteration:
##   1. Retrieve pre-sampled weights → renormalise to sum to 1
##   2. Multiply each species' continuous suitability by its normalised weight
##   3. Sum across species to get the disease group exposure index
##
## No threshold is applied; suitability values enter the index directly.
## This preserves ecological gradients and eliminates binary classification
## artefacts at threshold boundaries.

	cat("Running Monte Carlo simulation (continuous approach)...\n")

	mc_results <- purrr::map(disease_groups, function(dg) {

		cat("  ", dg, "...\n")

		## Species in this disease group
		group_spec    <- disease_weights |> dplyr::filter(disease_group == dg)
		group_species <- group_spec$species

		## Pre-allocate result matrix (municipalities × iterations)
		result_mat <- matrix(
			NA_real_,
			nrow     = n_municipalities,
			ncol     = N_ITERATIONS,
			dimnames = list(municipalities$NAME_2, NULL)
		)

		## Vectorised municipality suitability values for this group's species
		## Matrix: municipalities (rows) × species (cols)
		suit_matrix <- purrr::map(group_species, function(sp) {
			suit_lookup[[sp]][municipalities$NAME_2]
		}) |>
			set_names(group_species) |>
			bind_cols() |>
			as.matrix()

		## Replace any NAs with 0 (missing extractions treated as unsuitable)
		suit_matrix[is.na(suit_matrix)] <- 0

		## Run all iterations
		purrr::walk(seq_len(N_ITERATIONS), function(iter) {

			## Retrieve and renormalise sampled weights for this iteration
			raw_weights <- purrr::map_dbl(group_species, function(sp) {
				key <- paste(dg, sp, sep = "::")
				weight_samples[[key]][iter]
			})
			norm_weights <- raw_weights / sum(raw_weights)

			## Weighted sum of continuous suitability values
			## Matrix multiplication: (n_muni × n_species) %*% (n_species × 1)
			result_mat[, iter] <<- as.numeric(suit_matrix %*% norm_weights)
		})

		result_mat
	}) |>
		set_names(disease_groups)

	cat("  Monte Carlo simulation complete.\n\n")


# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# SUMMARISE MC RESULTS
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

	disease_exposure <- purrr::map_dfr(disease_groups, function(dg) {

		mat <- mc_results[[dg]]

		tibble(
			disease_group = dg,
			NAME_2        = municipalities$NAME_2,
			GID_2         = municipalities$GID_2,
			exposure_mean = rowMeans(mat, na.rm = TRUE),
			exposure_sd   = apply(mat, 1, sd, na.rm = TRUE),
			exposure_q025 = apply(mat, 1, quantile, probs = 0.025, na.rm = TRUE),
			exposure_q975 = apply(mat, 1, quantile, probs = 0.975, na.rm = TRUE)
		)
	}) |>
		left_join(disease_labels, by = "disease_group")


	cat("══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n")
	cat("  DISEASE EXPOSURE SUMMARY — CONTINUOUS (Baseline)\n")
	cat("══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n\n")

	disease_exposure |>
		group_by(disease_group, disease_label) |>
		summarise(
			mean_exposure    = round(mean(exposure_mean), 4),
			sd_exposure      = round(mean(exposure_sd), 4),
			min_exposure     = round(min(exposure_mean), 4),
			max_exposure     = round(max(exposure_mean), 4),
			n_municipalities = n(),
			.groups = "drop"
		) |>
		print(n = 20, width = Inf)


# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# WEIGHT SENSITIVITY — COEFFICIENT OF VARIATION
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

	cat("\n\n══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n")
	cat("  WEIGHT SENSITIVITY — COEFFICIENT OF VARIATION\n")
	cat("══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n\n")

	sensitivity_summary <- disease_exposure |>
		mutate(
			cv = if_else(exposure_mean > 0, exposure_sd / exposure_mean, NA_real_)
		) |>
		group_by(disease_group, disease_label) |>
		summarise(
			mean_cv   = round(mean(cv, na.rm = TRUE), 4),
			median_cv = round(median(cv, na.rm = TRUE), 4),
			max_cv    = round(max(cv, na.rm = TRUE), 4),
			.groups   = "drop"
		) |>
		arrange(desc(mean_cv))

	print(sensitivity_summary, n = 20, width = Inf)


# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# RANK STABILITY DIAGNOSTIC
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
## For each disease group, compute the Spearman rank correlation between
## the point estimate and each MC iteration to assess whether the spatial
## ranking of municipalities is stable across weight perturbations.
## A mean rho > 0.95 indicates that ordinal rankings are effectively
## invariant to weight uncertainty.

	cat("\n\n══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n")
	cat("  RANK STABILITY — SPEARMAN CORRELATION WITH POINT ESTIMATE\n")
	cat("══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n\n")

	rank_stability <- purrr::map_dfr(disease_groups, function(dg) {

		mat       <- mc_results[[dg]]
		point_est <- rowMeans(mat, na.rm = TRUE)

		## Spearman rho between point estimate and each iteration
		iter_rhos <- purrr::map_dbl(seq_len(N_ITERATIONS), function(iter) {
			cor(point_est, mat[, iter], method = "spearman", use = "complete.obs")
		})

		tibble(
			disease_group = dg,
			rho_mean      = round(mean(iter_rhos, na.rm = TRUE), 4),
			rho_sd        = round(sd(iter_rhos, na.rm = TRUE), 4),
			rho_min       = round(min(iter_rhos, na.rm = TRUE), 4)
		)
	}) |>
		left_join(disease_labels, by = "disease_group")

	print(rank_stability, n = 20, width = Inf)

	cat("\n  Interpretation:\n")
	cat("    rho > 0.99 → Rankings are essentially invariant to weight changes\n")
	cat("    rho > 0.95 → Rankings are highly stable\n")
	cat("    rho < 0.90 → Rankings shift meaningfully with weight perturbation\n\n")


# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# SAVE OUTPUTS
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

	## Long format
	write_csv(
		disease_exposure,
		file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "disease_exposure_continuous_mc_baseline.csv")
	)
	cat("  ✓ disease_exposure_continuous_mc_baseline.csv\n")

	## Wide format
	disease_exposure_wide <- disease_exposure |>
		dplyr::select(NAME_2, GID_2, disease_group, exposure_mean) |>
		pivot_wider(
			names_from  = disease_group,
			values_from = exposure_mean,
			names_prefix = "exposure_"
		)

	write_csv(
		disease_exposure_wide,
		file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "disease_exposure_continuous_mc_baseline_wide.csv")
	)
	cat("  ✓ disease_exposure_continuous_mc_baseline_wide.csv\n")

	## Sensitivity and rank stability
	write_csv(
		sensitivity_summary,
		file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "weight_sensitivity_cv_continuous.csv")
	)
	cat("  ✓ weight_sensitivity_cv_continuous.csv\n")

	write_csv(
		rank_stability,
		file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "rank_stability_continuous.csv")
	)
	cat("  ✓ rank_stability_continuous.csv\n")

	cat("\nAll outputs saved to:", OUTPUT_DIR, "\n")
```

```{r Load in Georgia Vulnerability Data}
  # LOAD GEORGIA VULNERABILITY DATA FROM GITHUB

  GITHUB_BASE <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/IanPsheaSmith/GVecVuln/main/data/georgia_census"

  COMPONENTS <- c(
      "population_total",
      "healthcare_staff",
      "education_graduates",
      "age_dependency",
      "disability_prevalence",
      "average_wages"
  )


  # LOAD METADATA FROM GITHUB

  #' Load municipality metadata from GitHub
    #' @return tibble with region, municipality_slug, and component availability
      load_municipalities_metadata <- function() {
          
          url <- glue("{GITHUB_BASE}/municipalities.csv")
          
          tryCatch({
              read_csv(url, show_col_types = FALSE)
          }, error = function(e) {
              stop("Failed to load municipalities.csv from GitHub. Check your internet connection.")
          })
      }

  # LOAD SINGLE FILE FROM GITHUB

  #' Load a single Excel file from GitHub
    #' @param region Region URL key (e.g., "tbilisi", "adjara")
    #' @param municipality_slug Municipality slug (e.g., "batumi")
    #' @param component Component name (e.g., "population_total")
    #' @return tibble with Excel data, or NULL if not found
      load_component_github <- function(region, municipality_slug, component) {
          
          url <- glue("{GITHUB_BASE}/{region}/{municipality_slug}/{component}.xlsx")
          
          # Download to temp file (required for read_excel)
          temp_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".xlsx")
          
          response <- tryCatch({
              GET(url, write_disk(temp_file, overwrite = TRUE), timeout(30))
          }, error = function(e) NULL)
          
          if (is.null(response) || status_code(response) != 200) {
              return(NULL)
          }
          
          tryCatch({
              read_excel(temp_file)
          }, error = function(e) {
              NULL
          }) %>%
              { if (!is.null(.)) mutate(., .region = region, .municipality = municipality_slug, .component = component) else NULL }
      }

  # LOAD ALL DATA FOR ONE MUNICIPALITY

    #' Load all 6 components for a single municipality
      #' @param region Region URL key
      #' @param municipality_slug Municipality slug
      #' @param verbose Print progress messages
      #' @return Named list of tibbles (one per component)
        load_municipality_github <- function(region, municipality_slug, verbose = TRUE) {
            
            if (verbose) cat(glue("Loading {region}/{municipality_slug}...\n"))
            
            results <- COMPONENTS %>%
                set_names() %>%
                map(function(comp) {
                    data <- load_component_github(region, municipality_slug, comp)
                    if (verbose && !is.null(data)) cat(glue("  ✓ {comp}\n"))
                    if (verbose && is.null(data)) cat(glue("  ✗ {comp} (not found)\n"))
                    data
                }) %>%
                compact()
            
            if (verbose) cat(glue("  Loaded {length(results)}/6 components\n\n"))
            
            results
        }

  # LOAD ALL DATA FOR ONE REGION
  
    #' Load all municipalities in a region
      #' @param region Region URL key
      #' @param verbose Print progress messages
      #' @return Nested list: region$municipality$component
        load_region_github <- function(region_name, verbose = TRUE) {
            
            metadata <- load_municipalities_metadata()
            
            # Fix: use region_name to avoid column/variable conflict
            region_munis <- metadata %>%
                filter(region == region_name) %>%
                pull(municipality_slug)
            
            if (length(region_munis) == 0) {
                stop(glue("Region '{region_name}' not found. Available: {str_c(unique(metadata$region), collapse = ', ')}"))
            }
            
            if (verbose) cat(glue("\n=== Loading {region_name}: {length(region_munis)} municipalities ===\n\n"))
            
            region_munis %>%
                set_names() %>%
                map(~ load_municipality_github(region_name, .x, verbose = verbose))
        }

  # LOAD ALL GEORGIA DATA
  
  #' Load complete dataset for all 64 municipalities
    #' @param verbose Print progress messages
    #' @return Nested list: region$municipality$component
      load_georgia_data <- function(verbose = TRUE) {
          
          metadata <- load_municipalities_metadata()
          regions  <- unique(metadata$region)
          
          if (verbose) {
              cat(glue("\n{'=' %>% strrep(60)}\n"))
              cat("LOADING GEORGIA VULNERABILITY DATA FROM GITHUB\n")
              cat(glue("{'=' %>% strrep(60)}\n"))
              cat(glue("\nTotal: {nrow(metadata)} municipalities across {length(regions)} regions\n\n"))
          }
          
          all_data <- regions %>%
              set_names() %>%
              map(~ load_region_github(.x, verbose = verbose))
          
          if (verbose) {
              total_loaded <- all_data %>%
                  map_int(~ sum(map_int(.x, length))) %>%
                  sum()
          }
          
          all_data
      }

  # FLATTEN TO SINGLE TIBBLE (LONG FORMAT)
  
  #' Convert nested data to single long-format tibble
    #' @param data Nested list from load_georgia_data()
    #' @param component Which component to extract (e.g., "population_total")
    #' @return Single tibble with all municipalities for that component
      flatten_component <- function(data, component) {
          
          data %>%
              imap_dfr(function(region_data, region_name) {
                  region_data %>%
                      imap_dfr(function(muni_data, muni_name) {
                          if (component %in% names(muni_data)) {
                              muni_data[[component]] %>%
                                  mutate(
                                      region       = region_name,
                                      municipality = muni_name,
                                      .before      = 1
                                  )
                          } else {
                              NULL
                          }
                      })
              })
      }

  # LIST AVAILABLE REGIONS AND MUNICIPALITIES
    #' List all available regions
      list_regions <- function() {
          metadata <- load_municipalities_metadata()
          
          metadata %>%
              group_by(region) %>%
              summarise(
                  municipalities = n(),
                  complete       = sum(complete),
                  .groups        = "drop"
              ) %>%
              arrange(region)
      }
      
      #' List municipalities in a region
        list_municipalities <- function(region) {
            metadata <- load_municipalities_metadata()
            
            metadata %>%
                filter(region == !!region) %>%
                dplyr::select(municipality_slug, n_components, complete)
        }
```
